source.excerpt: Your people, sir,—your people is a great beast!
trail: Wikiquote quotes the 1859 Memoir of Theophilus Parsons and its explicit hearsay chain: the writer heard it from a friend, who heard it from a guest. The memoir’s own caveat leaves open whether the remark was a jest. That is not direct verification of Hamilton’s words. The anecdote and its warning ↗
The article reports Stephen Knott’s criticism of the anecdote’s transmission. Discussion of the legend ↗

author.heading: About Alexander Hamilton
author.bio: Hamilton’s political reputation has often been argued through both his published work and anecdotes about his private speech. This particular anecdote survives in another family’s memoir rather than Hamilton’s own papers.

context.heading: Why it mattered
lead: The dinner-table remark was printed in an 1859 memoir through a chain of recollection. The account leaves the circumstances and tone uncertain, so it cannot safely be treated as a carefully stated principle from a published Hamilton essay.
